catalog_citation: Perekhvalskaya, Elena. 2021. Grammatical functions of tone in San Maka. Mandenkan 65: 333-348. doi:10.4000/mandenkan.2574 (publisher PDF)
catalog_locator: p. 336, section 2.1.5 'Tonal system'; parallel statement Perekhvalskaya 2017, Mandenkan 57, p. 53, section 2.1.2, and Perekhvalskaya 2017b, Afrikanskij sbornik 2017, p. 436 fn. 3
catalog_quote: San Maka is a tonal language with three level tones, designated, according to the IPA, by diacritics: acute (high), macron (mid) and grave (low). Vowel sequences may bear the following combinations of tones: level cv́v́; cv̄v̄; cv̀v̀ / falling cv́v̀; cv́v̄; cv̄v̀ / rising cv̀v́; cv̄v́ / Susanne Platiel focused on distribution of tonal units according to the types of syllables and words. She showed that words of the CVCV structure cannot carry the mid tone in both syllables if they contain closed or semi-closed vowels: /i/, /u/, /e/, /o/ (Platiel 1974: 132). Platiel also pointed out the rarity of tonal minimal pairs and triplets: it is difficult to find three or four identical segment chains that would differ only by tone
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.rule_in_words: San Maka (Southern Samo) is a three-level tone language (H, M, L, plus contour combinations on vowel sequences); tone is lexically and grammatically distinctive. Neither of the two accessible modern descriptions (Perekhvalskaya 2017, 2021) mentions word stress, accent or metrical prominence at all; no statement about where stress falls exists in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress (source is silent). Tonal restriction noted: CVCV words with close/half-close vowels cannot be M-M (Platiel 1974: 132).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level tone description; citation forms of nouns and verbs (neutral form is the dictionary form). Nothing on phrase-level prominence or intonation.
new_statements.identity_note: Perekhvalskaya's 'San Maka' / 'Southern San (san-maka)' is the southern variety of the San/Samo cluster (Toma area, Nayala province), the same variety as Platiel's 'parler samo de Toma' and Ki's 'san du sud ou parler de Toma'; Glottolog files all of these under sout2844 Southern Samo [sbd]. Northern varieties (Matya stj, Maya sym) are separate languages with low mutual intelligibility. Glottolog's Daniel & Shaw 1977 'Samo phonemes' is Papua New Guinea Samo, misassigned.

tone_statements.quote: San Maka is a tonal language with three level tones, designated, according to the IPA, by diacritics: acute (high), macron (mid) and grave (low). tone_statements.summary: San Maka (Southern Samo): three level tones H, M, L on the syllable/vowel, contour melodies only on vowel sequences, lexical function plus heavy grammatical (aspectual, pronominal, derivational) tone; no stress or accent mentioned.

tone_statements.citation: Platiel, Suzy [Suzanne]. 1983. Les procédés de formation des noms en san: dérivation et composition. Mandenkan 6: 75-89.
tone_statements.quote: Remarque: On notera que dans presque tous les exemples cités présentant deux noms se suivant immédiatement, le second subit un relèvement tonal par rapport à son ton de base : “le nom” ----> tɔ à ton moyen qui prend un ton haut dans pérä-tɔ Ce changement de ton est conforme à la règle qui s'applique dans tous les cas de syntagmes nominaux servant à exprimer une caractérisation .
tone_statements.translation: Note: in almost all the examples cited with two nouns in immediate succession, the second undergoes a tonal raising relative to its basic tone: 'the name' -> tɔ with mid tone, which takes a high tone in pérä-tɔ. This change of tone conforms to the rule that applies in all cases of noun phrases expressing a characterisation.
tone_statements.locator: p. 84 (under the page number '- 84 -'), 'Remarque' closing the section on composition, before 'La composition systématique'; : 'reléve-\nment' dehyphenated and accent normalised to 'relèvement'
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Three registers (bas, moyen, haut) referred to; contour ('mélodique') tones arise on monosyllables under reduplication; grammatical/derivational tone: H-toned diminutive suffix, M-toned suffix, tone raising of the second noun in noun+noun (characterisation) phrases, one-register lowering of unpossessed body-part nouns and of readers=patient verb forms.

tone.says: First-hand description (own fieldwork, RSF 'Tonal languages of the world' project) of the SOUTHERN sibling: three level tones H/M/L, contours only as sequences on vowel sequences, few lexical minimal pairs (after Platiel 1974), and a catalogue of grammatical tone: neutral vs perfective verb forms distinguished by tone, low-tone allomorph of the 3sg inanimate object pronoun, tonal allomorph of the perfective predicative marker, tone in derivation. Nothing first-hand on Makya/Matya tone.

sources.citation: Platiel, Suzy [Suzanne]. 1981. La formation des verbes en san. Mandenkan 2: 69-83.
sources.quote: l'ommission du deuxième participant est marquée par un changement de ton du procès, ce qui exprime l'amalgame avec le Pronom personnel 3ème personne du singulier / à / ; ainsi on aura [...] cette femme a fait tomber le canari [...] mais on aura, avec changement de ton sur tomber : [...] le canri [sic, scanned; = canari] est tombé
sources.locator: pp. 73-74 (-4 of 8 of a page without printed header, position fixed between the '72' and '76' page numbers), section 'Application au san', 2-b
sources.note: A syntactic-semantic account of how San builds verb concepts from a small stock of verb radicals plus nominal participants. Tone enters once: verbs are cited in three aspectual forms (acc., inac., zero, e.g. bɔ-bée-bɔ 'enlever', footnote 2) and, for two-participant verbs, omission of the second participant 'est marquée par un changement de ton du procès' (amalgam with the 3sg pronoun à), illustrated with 'faire tomber' vs 'tomber'. No tone inventory or tone rules beyond this.
